ingredients: 450 g button or cup mushrooms (2 punnets), whole
60–125 ml thickened or pure cream (1/4–1/2 cup)
method: Rinse the mushrooms and dry them well with a clean tea towel.
Mince the garlic and dice the onion.
Melt the butter in a heavy-based frying pan over medium heat without letting it burn.
Add the garlic and onion and cook for about 1 minute, stirring so nothing burns.
Turn the heat up, add the mushrooms and season with salt.
Stir often for 2–3 minutes, lowering the heat if needed.
Pour in the cream and milk, add the cayenne or paprika, and simmer about 2 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Take off the heat once the sauce is as thick as you like.
Sprinkle with parsley and chilli flakes and serve straight away.
name: Creamy garlic mushrooms
tips: No-cream version: skip the cream and milk. Once the mushrooms are golden, add a splash of soy sauce or tamari and fresh thyme, and finish with lemon juice.
Use 1/4 onion and 5 garlic cloves to drop to about 6 g net carbs a serve.
Make it a main by serving it on a steak or with sliced chicken thigh.
verdict: Keto friendly as a side. Most of the carbs come from the garlic and onion, not the mushrooms. Low in protein, so pair it with steak, chicken or eggs. Don't serve it over rice or pasta like the original suggests, as that would spike your blood sugar.
warnings: Low in protein on its own. Serve with steak, chicken or eggs.
alt: Whole mushrooms in a creamy garlic sauce with parsley and chilli flakes

ingredients: 1 kg pork belly, skin on, boneless
method: The day before (or at least 2 hours ahead), score the skin, pat it very dry and leave uncovered in the fridge.
Rub the meat side (not the skin) with five spice and 1 tbsp tamari. Rub salt into the skin.
Roast at 160°C fan for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Turn up to 230°C and roast 20–30 minutes until the skin crackles all over. Rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir-fry the garlic in sesame oil, add the bok choy and the rest of the tamari, and cook 2–3 minutes.
Slice the pork and serve with the bok choy.
name: Crispy pork belly with garlic bok choy
tips: Leftover slices are great in the kimchi stew.
verdict: Pork belly is close to zero carbs. Have it with greens or cauliflower rice, not white rice. Use tamari or soy sauce, and skip sweet sauces like hoisin or char siu.
warnings: High in calories (about 600 a serve) and saturated fat. Stick to one serve.
alt: Slices of roast pork belly with golden crackling and garlic bok choy

ingredients: 2 salmon fillets, skin on (about 180 g each)
method: Pat the salmon skin very dry and season with salt.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the salmon skin side down for 5–6 minutes, pressing gently, until the skin is crisp.
Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more. Set aside.
Steam or blanch the broccolini for 2–3 minutes.
In the same pan, melt the butter with the garlic until it foams. Add the lemon juice.
Plate the salmon and broccolini and spoon the lemon butter over.
name: Crispy skin salmon with lemon butter and broccolini
tips: Swap in ocean trout or barramundi when they're on special.
verdict: High in protein and healthy fats, low in carbs. A good regular fish night that's easier to sustain than sashimi.
alt: Crispy-skin salmon fillet with broccolini in lemon garlic butter

ingredients: 400 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined (frozen is fine)
1 long red chilli, sliced (or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes)
method: Pat the prawns dry and season with salt.
Melt half the butter in a large pan over high heat. Cook the prawns 1–2 minutes a side until just pink, then set aside.
Lower the heat, add the rest of the butter, the garlic and chilli and cook 1 minute.
Add the zucchini noodles and toss 2 minutes until just soft.
Return the prawns, add the lemon juice and parsley and toss. Serve.
name: Garlic butter prawns with zucchini noodles
tips: Add a few sliced mushrooms with the garlic for extra bulk.
Don't overcook the zucchini or it goes watery.
verdict: Prawns are zero carb and cheaper than sashimi. The zucchini noodles stand in for pasta. Frozen Australian prawns work well and keep costs down.
alt: Pink garlic butter prawns with spiralised zucchini, chilli and parsley

ingredients: 1 thick beef or pork sausage, 90%+ meat, gluten free (about 70 g)
method: Fry the sausage over medium heat for about 12 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Add the bacon and the tomato (cut side down) to the same pan and cook 3–4 minutes.
Push everything to one side, add the butter and the mushrooms and cook until golden.
Wilt the spinach in the pan for 30 seconds.
Fry the eggs in the leftover fat to your liking. Season and serve.
name: Keto full English breakfast
tips: Swap the tomato for extra mushrooms to save about 1.5 g carbs.
Add black pudding only if it's a low-filler one. Most use oats and are high in carbs.
verdict: Everything you love about a fry-up, minus the toast, baked beans and hash brown, which are the parts that spike blood sugar. Check the sausage label: cheap sausages use breadcrumbs or rusk.
warnings: High in calories (about 600 a plate).
Bacon and sausages are processed and salty. Best as a weekend treat, not daily.
alt: Fried eggs, bacon, sausage, mushrooms, grilled tomato and spinach

ingredients: 300 g well-fermented kimchi (no added sugar), chopped, plus 3 tbsp of its juice
1 tsp gochujang (optional, no more than this)
300 g firm tofu, cut into cubes
method: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Fry the pork belly 3–4 minutes until it starts to brown.
Add the kimchi, onion and garlic and fry 5 minutes.
Stir in the gochugaru, gochujang (if using), tamari and kimchi juice.
Pour in the water or stock, bring to the boil, then simmer 15–20 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer 5 more minutes.
Top with spring onion and serve hot, without rice.
name: Kimchi stew with pork belly (kimchi jjigae)
tips: Crack an egg into each bowl in the last 3 minutes for extra protein.
Older, sourer kimchi has less sugar and more flavour.
verdict: Keto friendly if you leave out the rice and use chilli flakes instead of most of the gochujang, which is high in sugar. Check the kimchi label for added sugar.
warnings: High in salt from the kimchi and soy. Use salt-reduced stock.
alt: Kimchi stew with sliced pork belly, tofu cubes and spring onions

ingredients: 1 tin sardines or mackerel in olive oil (about 110 g), drained
Pinch of chilli flakes, salt and pepper
method: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Smash the avocado with lemon, salt and pepper.
Plate the rocket, cucumber, avocado, halved eggs and sardines.
Finish with chilli flakes and a drizzle of oil from the tin.
name: Sardine, egg and avocado plate
tips: Try smoked mussels or salmon in springwater for variety.
Check flavoured tins (tomato sauce, sweet chilli) for added sugar.
verdict: A cheap, no-cook lunch. Tinned sardines or mackerel give you the omega-3s of sashimi for a few dollars a tin.
alt: Sardines, jammy boiled eggs, sliced avocado, cucumber and rocket

ingredients: 200 g scotch fillet, at room temperature
Chimichurri: 1/2 cup flat-leaf parsley, 1 garlic clove, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, pinch of chilli flakes, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 20 ml extra virgin olive oil, salt
method: Finely chop the parsley and garlic and mix with the oregano, chilli, vinegar, oil and salt. Let it sit while you cook.
Pat the steak dry and season with salt.
Sear in a very hot pan 2–3 minutes a side for medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry the eggs in butter in the same pan.
Slice the steak, top with chimichurri and serve with the eggs and rocket.
name: Steak and eggs with chimichurri
tips: Make a jar of chimichurri on Sunday. It keeps 5 days in the fridge.
verdict: Almost no carbs and very filling. A big plate, so it can easily be your main meal of the day.
warnings: High in calories (about 735 a plate). Make it the main meal of the day.
alt: Sliced steak topped with chimichurri beside two fried eggs and rocket

ingredients: 300 g beef eye fillet, very cold
1 Lebanese cucumber, thickly sliced, to serve
method: Trim any sinew from the beef and dice it finely by hand (don't mince it).
Mix the eschalot, capers, cornichons, mustard, Worcestershire, Tabasco, oil and parsley in a bowl.
Fold the beef through and season well.
Shape into two rounds on plates, make a small well on top and drop in an egg yolk.
Serve straight away with cucumber slices.
name: Steak tartare with cucumber crisps
tips: Add a few drops of fish sauce or a little anchovy for extra depth with no carbs.
verdict: Very low carb and high protein. Serve on cucumber slices or lettuce cups instead of toast or chips. Use very fresh, good-quality beef from a butcher you trust.
warnings: Raw beef and raw egg yolk. Buy very fresh beef from a butcher and make it the day you buy it.
alt: Finely diced beef tartare topped with an egg yolk and surrounded by cucumber rounds

name: Chanko nabe with chicken meatballs and mushrooms
verdict: A light, brothy sumo hotpot that's high in protein and easy on blood sugar. Skip the udon or rice usually added at the end. Freezes well without the tofu.
ingredients: Meatballs: 500 g chicken thigh mince, 1 egg, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 1 spring onion finely chopped, 1 tbsp tamari or soy sauce, pinch of salt
2 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
method: Mix the meatball ingredients well with your hands. Chill 10 minutes if it's soft.
Bring the stock, tamari and sake to a simmer in a wide pot.
Roll heaped tablespoons of mince into balls and drop them into the broth. Simmer 8 minutes.
Add the wombok stems and shiitake and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the tofu, wombok leaves, bok choy, enoki and spring onion and simmer 3 to 4 minutes more.
Serve at the table straight from the pot.
tips: Make a double batch of meatballs and freeze half raw for next time.
Add sliced pork belly or prawns for a bigger pot.
warnings: Can be salty. Use salt-reduced stock and taste before adding more soy.
alt: Japanese hotpot with chicken meatballs, tofu, mushrooms and greens

name: Pork and kimchi hotpot with mushrooms
verdict: A spicy army-stew style hotpot without the ramen noodles, baked beans or processed meats that push the carbs up. Keep the gochujang to 1 teaspoon.
ingredients: 300 g well-fermented kimchi (no added sugar), chopped
200 g mixed mushrooms (shiitake, oyster or king brown), sliced
method: Mix the gochugaru, gochujang, garlic and tamari into a paste.
Arrange the pork, kimchi, cabbage, mushrooms and tofu in sections in a wide shallow pot. Put the paste in the middle.
Pour in the stock and bring to the boil, then simmer 10 to 12 minutes until the pork is cooked.
Crack the eggs into the broth, add the enoki and simmer 3 minutes.
Top with spring onion and serve at the table.
tips: Swap the pork for leftover crispy pork belly from the recipe on this page.
Add a handful of spinach at the end for more greens.
warnings: High in salt from the kimchi and soy.
Fairly high in calories (about 565 a serve).
alt: Red kimchi hotpot with pork belly, mushrooms, tofu and poached eggs

name: Shabu shabu hotpot
verdict: Fun to eat at the table and very low carb. Bottled ponzu and sesame dipping sauces often have added sugar, so make the simple dipping sauce below instead.
ingredients: 600 g shabu shabu beef (very thinly sliced scotch fillet, from an Asian grocer)
Dipping sauce: 4 tbsp tamari or soy sauce, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp grated ginger, sliced spring onion
method: Soak the kombu in the water for 30 minutes, then bring it slowly to a simmer and remove the kombu just before it boils.
Mix the dipping sauce and divide into small bowls.
Arrange the beef and vegetables on platters.
Keep the broth simmering at the table (a portable burner works best). Add vegetables, tofu and mushrooms first.
Each person swishes a slice of beef in the broth for 10 to 20 seconds until just cooked, then dips it in the sauce.
Drink the rich broth at the end as soup.
tips: Use thinly sliced pork belly instead of beef for a change.
Leftover broth makes a great base for the egg drop soup.
alt: Japanese hotpot with tofu, mushrooms and greens beside thinly sliced marbled beef

name: Pork and mushroom miso soup
verdict: A hearty Japanese pork miso soup (tonjiru) without the potato and carrot. Miso has some carbs, so stick to about 3 tablespoons for the pot. Freezes well; add the miso when you reheat if you can.
ingredients: 3 tbsp white or red miso paste
200 g mixed mushrooms (shiitake and shimeji or oyster), sliced
100 g daikon (white radish), cut into thin half-moons
Shichimi or chilli flakes, to serve
method: Heat the sesame oil in a pot and fry the pork 3 minutes until it starts to brown.
Add the mushrooms and daikon and fry 2 minutes.
Pour in the dashi, bring to the boil, skim off any foam and simmer 10 minutes until the daikon is tender.
Add the tofu and cabbage and simmer 3 minutes.
Turn the heat to low. Mix the miso with a ladle of broth until smooth, then stir it in. Don't let it boil after this.
Serve topped with spring onion and shichimi.
tips: Use pork shoulder instead of belly for a leaner soup with more protein.
warnings: High in salt from the miso and dashi. Use salt-reduced dashi or stock.
alt: Miso soup with sliced pork belly, mushrooms, daikon, cabbage and tofu

name: Mushroom egg drop soup
verdict: Ready in 5 to 10 minutes and very low carb. It's light, so add shredded chicken or prawns to make it a meal. Restaurant versions are thickened with cornflour; this one isn't.
method: Bring the stock, ginger, tamari and mushrooms to a simmer and cook 3 minutes.
Stir the soup in a circle, then slowly pour in the beaten eggs in a thin stream so they form ribbons.
Leave it for 30 seconds, then stir gently.
Add the sesame oil, white pepper and spring onion and serve.
tips: Add 150 g shredded cooked chicken to bring the protein up to about 30 g a serve.
Leftover shabu shabu broth makes it even better.
warnings: Low in protein and calories on its own. Add chicken or prawns to make it a meal.
alt: Fine egg ribbons, sliced shiitake mushrooms and spring onions in golden broth

name: Mushroom and spinach omelette
method: Melt half the butter in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and cook the mushrooms 3 minutes until golden. Add the spinach until it wilts, then tip out.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the rest of the butter, pour in the eggs and stir gently for 20 seconds, then let it set.
Spoon the mushrooms and spinach over one half, fold over and slide onto a plate. Top with chives.
tips: Add a few slices of ham or leftover steak for a bigger meal.
alt: Folded omelette filled with mushrooms and spinach and topped with chives

name: Korean steamed egg (gyeran jjim)
ingredients: 1 tsp fish sauce or 1/2 tsp salt
Pinch of chilli flakes and sesame seeds
method: Whisk the eggs, stock and fish sauce until smooth.
Pour into a small heatproof bowl or claypot and stir in most of the spring onion.
Steam over simmering water, covered, for 10 to 12 minutes until just set and puffy (or cook in a small pot on low heat with the lid on).
Drizzle with sesame oil and top with the rest of the spring onion, chilli and sesame seeds.
tips: Great next to bulgogi or pork belly.
alt: Fluffy Korean steamed egg with spring onions in a black earthenware bowl

name: Soy-marinated eggs
ingredients: 1 tbsp granulated sweetener (optional, instead of sugar)
method: Boil the eggs for 6 1/2 minutes for jammy yolks, then put them straight into iced water. Peel.
Mix the tamari, water, sweetener, garlic, chilli and spring onion in a container.
Add the eggs, cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight. Sprinkle with sesame seeds to serve.
tips: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Great with the steamed egg or in soups.
warnings: The marinade is very salty. Eat 1 or 2 at a time and don't drink the marinade.
alt: Halved soy-marinated eggs with jammy yolks, chilli, spring onion and sesame

name: Bacon and egg cups
method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Spray 6 holes of a muffin tin.
Line each hole with a bacon rasher to make a cup. Add a little spinach.
Crack an egg into each and season.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes until the whites are set. Top with chives.
tips: Make a batch on Sunday. They keep 3 days in the fridge and reheat in 30 seconds.
warnings: Bacon is processed and salty. Fine a few times a week, not every day.
alt: Baked eggs in bacon cups with spinach and chopped chives

name: Beef bulgogi lettuce cups
ingredients: 600 g scotch fillet or rump, very thinly sliced (or bulgogi beef from an Asian grocer)
1 tsp granulated sweetener (optional, instead of sugar and pear)
Kimchi and sesame seeds, to serve
method: Mix the tamari, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, sweetener and pepper. Toss through the beef and leave 30 minutes (or overnight).
Heat a large frying pan until very hot. Cook the beef in two batches for 2 to 3 minutes until browned.
Toss through the spring onion.
Serve in lettuce leaves with cucumber, kimchi and sesame seeds.
tips: Pork shoulder slices work too (that's dwaeji bulgogi). Add 1 tsp gochugaru for spice.
alt: Butter lettuce cups filled with sliced bulgogi beef, cucumber and kimchi

name: Pork larb lettuce cups
ingredients: 1 stalk lemongrass, finely chopped (or 1 tbsp paste)
1 iceberg or cos lettuce, leaves separated
method: Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat. Add the pork and lemongrass and cook 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked and a little crispy.
Take off the heat. Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, chilli and eschalots.
Toss through the herbs and spring onion.
Spoon into lettuce cups and serve with cucumber.
tips: Chicken or beef mince work just as well.
The traditional version uses toasted rice powder; leave it out.
alt: Lettuce cups filled with minced pork larb and fresh herbs, served with cucumber

name: Sheet-pan chicken thighs with mushrooms and broccoli
ingredients: 8 chicken thighs, bone in and skin on (about 1.2 kg)
400 g mushrooms (cup or Swiss brown), halved
1 head broccoli (about 400 g), cut into florets
method: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced.
Rub the chicken with half the oil, salt and pepper and put skin side up on a large tray. Roast 20 minutes.
Toss the mushrooms, broccoli and garlic with the rest of the oil and add to the tray with the herbs and lemon.
Roast 20 minutes more until the skin is crisp and the chicken is cooked through. Squeeze the roasted lemon over.
tips: One tray, almost no washing up. Leftovers are great in the egg drop soup.
warnings: Fairly high in calories (about 545 a serve) because of the skin. Remove the skin for a lighter meal.
alt: Roasted chicken thighs, mushrooms, broccoli and lemon on a sheet pan

name: Garlic chilli calamari
method: Cut the squid open, score the inside in a criss-cross pattern and cut into pieces. Pat dry and season.
Heat a large frying pan until smoking. Add half the oil and the squid and cook 1 to 2 minutes until it curls and turns white. Don't overcook.
Lower the heat, add the rest of the oil, garlic and chilli for 30 seconds.
Squeeze in lemon, toss through parsley and serve on rocket.
tips: Frozen squid tubes from the supermarket are cheap and work well.
alt: Crosshatched calamari with red chilli and garlic on a bed of rocket

name: Tuna-stuffed avocado
ingredients: 1 tin tuna in olive oil (95 g), drained
Pinch of chilli flakes, salt and pepper
method: Mix the tuna, cucumber, capers, spring onion, lemon, chilli, salt and pepper.
Pile into the avocado halves and eat with a spoon.
tips: Swap the tuna for tinned salmon or smoked trout.
alt: Two avocado halves stuffed with flaked tuna, diced cucumber and spring onion

name: Prosciutto-wrapped asparagus
ingredients: 1 bunch asparagus (about 12 spears), woody ends snapped off
Lemon wedges and pepper, to serve
method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced.
Wrap each spear in a strip of prosciutto. Lay on a tray and drizzle with oil.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until the prosciutto is crisp. Serve with lemon and pepper.
tips: Also good wrapped around green beans or with a soft-boiled egg for dipping.
warnings: Prosciutto is cured and salty. Keep it to snack-sized portions.
alt: Roasted asparagus spears individually wrapped in prosciutto with lemon wedges

name: Dark chocolate nut bark
ingredients: 200 g dark chocolate, 85% cocoa or higher (e.g. Lindt 90%)
method: Line a tray with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate in a bowl over simmering water (or in 20-second bursts in the microwave).
Spread thinly on the tray and scatter over the nuts, seeds and salt.
Refrigerate 1 hour until set, then break into 12 pieces. Keep in the fridge.
tips: Freeze half so it's not all in reach.
warnings: High in calories (about 150 a piece). Stick to 1 or 2 pieces.
Use 85% cocoa or higher. 70% chocolate has much more sugar.
alt: Dark chocolate bark studded with almonds, macadamias and pumpkin seeds

name: Coffee jelly
ingredients: 500 ml strong black coffee (decaf for evenings)
Optional: a splash of unsweetened almond milk to serve
method: Sprinkle the gelatine over 60 ml of the coffee and leave 5 minutes to soften.
Heat the rest of the coffee until hot but not boiling. Stir in the softened gelatine and sweetener until dissolved.
Pour into 4 small glasses or a dish and refrigerate 3 hours until set.
Serve as is, or cut into cubes with a splash of almond milk.
tips: A light Japanese-style dessert that's almost zero carb.
warnings: Contains caffeine. Use decaf if you're having it at night.
alt: Dark coffee jelly cubes in a glass with a splash of almond milk

name: Dark chocolate strawberries
ingredients: 250 g strawberries, washed and dried well
method: Line a plate with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil.
Dip each strawberry halfway, let the extra drip off and put on the plate.
Chill 15 minutes until set.
tips: Raspberries are even lower in carbs if you want to swap.
warnings: Strawberries have natural sugar. Stick to about 4 or 5 berries a serve.
alt: Fresh strawberries dipped halfway in dark chocolate

name: Spicy Korean pork stir-fry (jeyuk)
ingredients: 600 g pork shoulder steaks or pork belly, thinly sliced
Lettuce leaves and sesame seeds, to serve
method: Mix the gochugaru, tamari, garlic, ginger, sweetener and sesame oil. Toss with the pork and leave 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat.
Add the pork and stir-fry 5 to 6 minutes until cooked and slightly charred.
Add the onion and cabbage and stir-fry 2 minutes. Toss through the spring onion.
Serve wrapped in lettuce leaves with sesame seeds.
tips: Gochugaru is at Coles, Woolworths (Asian aisle) or Amazon.
The restaurant version uses gochujang and sugar; this one keeps the heat without the sugar.

name: Japanese ginger pork (shogayaki)
ingredients: 400 g pork loin steaks, thinly sliced
Lemon wedge and spring onion, to serve
method: Mix the tamari, ginger and sake.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat. Fry the onion 2 minutes.
Add the pork in one layer and cook 1 to 2 minutes a side until browned.
Pour in the ginger sauce and toss until the pork is glazed, about 1 minute.
Serve on a pile of shredded cabbage with lemon and spring onion.
tips: Bagged coleslaw mix (no dressing) saves shredding the cabbage.

name: Steak with mushroom and thyme pan sauce
ingredients: 2 sirloin or porterhouse steaks (about 200 g each)
method: Take the steaks out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead. Pat dry and season well.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan until very hot. Cook the steaks 3 minutes a side for medium-rare. Rest on a plate.
Lower the heat, add the butter, mushrooms, garlic and thyme and cook 4 to 5 minutes until golden.
Pour in the stock and Worcestershire and bubble 2 minutes until it reduces a little. Add any resting juices.
Meanwhile, steam or boil the green beans 3 minutes.
Slice the steak and spoon the mushroom sauce over.
tips: No cream needed: the stock reduction gives a glossy sauce.

name: Beef and broccoli stir-fry
verdict: Oyster sauce has a little sugar, so 1 tablespoon for the whole pan is plenty.
ingredients: 1 head broccoli (about 400 g), cut into florets
Sesame seeds and sliced chilli, to serve
method: Mix the tamari, oyster sauce, garlic, ginger and sesame oil with 3 tbsp water.
Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the beef in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes, then set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and the broccoli with a splash of water. Cover and cook 3 minutes.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce and toss 1 minute. Sprinkle in the xanthan gum if you want it thicker.
Serve with sesame seeds and chilli. Have it on its own or with cauliflower rice.
tips: Xanthan gum is in the health food aisle at Coles and Woolworths, or on Amazon.

name: Korean beef and radish soup (soegogi muguk)
verdict: A light, clean Korean soup. Good alongside a heavier main.
ingredients: 300 g beef chuck or topside, thinly sliced
400 g daikon (white radish), cut into thin squares
method: Heat the sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Fry the beef and garlic 3 minutes.
Add the daikon and fry 2 minutes more.
Pour in the water, bring to the boil and skim off any foam.
Simmer 25 minutes until the radish is soft and see-through.
Season with fish sauce, tamari, salt and pepper. Top with spring onion.
tips: Freezes well. Add a soft-boiled egg or extra beef to make it a bigger meal.
Daikon is at most Coles and Woolworths in the fresh veg section.

name: Steamed barramundi with ginger and spring onion
ingredients: 2 barramundi fillets (about 180 g each), skin on
3 cm piece ginger, cut into thin matchsticks
4 spring onions, cut into thin strips
method: Put the fish on a heatproof plate and scatter over half the ginger.
Steam over boiling water, covered, for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes. Steam the bok choy alongside for the last 3 minutes.
Pour off any liquid from the plate. Top the fish with the rest of the ginger and the spring onion.
Heat the vegetable and sesame oil in a small pan until just smoking and pour it over the fish so it sizzles.
Drizzle with tamari and top with coriander.
tips: No steamer? Wrap the fish in foil and bake at 200°C fan-forced for 12 minutes.
Snapper or salmon work too.

name: Salmon poke bowl on cauliflower rice
ingredients: 300 g sashimi-grade salmon, cut into cubes (or hot-smoked salmon)
method: Microwave or pan-fry the cauliflower rice as per the packet and let it cool a little.
Mix the tamari, sesame oil and ginger. Toss half through the salmon.
Divide the cauliflower rice between two bowls.
Top with salmon, avocado, cucumber, spring onion, nori, sesame seeds and chilli. Drizzle over the rest of the dressing.
tips: Frozen cauliflower rice is in the freezer section at Coles and Woolworths.
Skip the pickled ginger and sweet mayo: both have added sugar.
warnings: Raw fish. Only use fish sold as sashimi-grade and eat it the day you buy it. Use hot-smoked salmon if unsure.

name: Chicken and shiitake skewers (shio yakitori)
ingredients: 800 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
200 g fresh shiitake mushrooms, stems removed
1 bunch spring onions, cut into 3 cm lengths
Lemon wedges and shichimi or chilli flakes, to serve
12 bamboo skewers, soaked in water 20 minutes
method: Thread chicken, spring onion and mushrooms onto the skewers.
Brush with oil and season well with salt.
Cook on a hot barbecue, grill pan or under the oven grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until the chicken is cooked and charred.
Serve with lemon and shichimi.
tips: Shio means salt: no sugary teriyaki sauce needed.
Leftovers are great cold in a lunchbox.

name: Prawn and mushroom egg foo young
verdict: The takeaway version uses a cornflour gravy; this one keeps it simple with a soy and sesame drizzle.
ingredients: Sauce: 1 tbsp tamari or soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp water
method: Beat the eggs with a pinch of white pepper. Stir in the prawns, bean sprouts, mushrooms and most of the spring onion.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Ladle in a third of the mix and cook 2 minutes a side until golden. Repeat to make 3 omelettes, adding oil as needed.
Warm the sauce ingredients in a small pan and spoon over. Top with the rest of the spring onion.
tips: Swap the prawns for leftover pork belly or chicken.

name: Clear tom yum with prawns and mushrooms
verdict: Low in calories and very light. Have it with a protein-heavy side if it's your main meal.
ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into lengths
4 slices fresh ginger (or galangal if you can find it)
400 g raw prawns, peeled with tails on
method: Bring the stock, lemongrass, lime leaves, ginger and chillies to the boil. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer 3 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook 2 to 3 minutes until pink.
Take off the heat and stir in the fish sauce and lime juice. Taste and add more of either.
Top with coriander and serve. Don't eat the lemongrass or lime leaves.
tips: Lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves are in the fresh herb section at Coles and Woolworths.
warnings: Can be salty from the fish sauce and stock. Use salt-reduced stock.
